transcript: The world population has passed 8 billion Yet more than 800 million people still lack enough food and suffer from hunger Agriculture is one of the oldest industries of humanity and a foundation of civilization. Since the invention of irrigation, farming in ancient Mesopotamia, humanity has multiplied crop yields many times, overthrew improved varieties and new technology. In the Green Revolution of the 20th Century, High yield varieties And chemical fertilizers Dramatically increased food production In Asia and Africa But at the same time The excessive use of pesticides And fertilizers has contaminated soil and water Causing long-term problems In recent years Both organic farming and genetically modified crops have drawn attention The former is kinder to the environment but difficult for mass production The latter raises yields but leaves concerns about safety Another major problem is food waste In developed countries About one third of all food produced is thrown away In a world where people go hungry, this is a serious contradiction Solving the food problem requires more than increasing production Improvement in distribution, reduction of waste And a change in the awareness of each consumer are all needed To feed the world in a sustainable way is the greatest challenge of the coming century

segments.text: The world population has passed 8 billion
Yet more than 800 million people still lack enough food and suffer from hunger
Agriculture is one of the oldest industries of humanity
and a foundation of civilization.
Since the invention of irrigation, farming in ancient Mesopotamia,
humanity has multiplied crop yields many times,
overthrew improved varieties and new technology.
In the Green Revolution of the 20th Century,
High yield varieties
And chemical fertilizers
Dramatically increased food production
In Asia and Africa
But at the same time
The excessive use of pesticides
And fertilizers has contaminated soil and water
Causing long-term problems
In recent years
Both organic farming
and genetically modified crops have drawn attention
The former is kinder to the environment but difficult for mass production
The latter raises yields but leaves concerns about safety
Another major problem is food waste
In developed countries
About one third of all food produced is thrown away
In a world where people go hungry, this is a serious contradiction
Solving the food problem requires more than increasing production
Improvement in distribution, reduction of waste
And a change in the awareness of each consumer are all needed
To feed the world in a sustainable way is the greatest challenge of the coming century
